course_name_original: Matemáticas aplicadas a la ingeniería mecánica

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire and understand the basic principles governing the behavior of dynamic systems, fundamental theorems, and resolution methods.
Describe the dynamic response of elementary mechanisms.
Know basic concepts and terminology in partial differential equations.
Model problems of heat transfer, fluid mechanics, and mechanical vibrations.
Understand the finite element method for analyzing mechanical components and structures.

syllabus_topics: Linear differential equations and systems of differential equations
Classical partial differential equations: Heat, wave, and Laplace equations
Mathematical models in heat transfer, mechanics and fluid dynamics, and mechanical vibrations
Solution of the associated homogeneous equation
Particular solution of the complete equation
Homogeneous linear systems of differential equations
Non-homogeneous linear systems of differential equations
Fourier series of an analytic function
First-order partial differential equations, method of characteristics
Second-order partial differential equations, method of separation of variables
Using Mathematica software for solving differential equations (Practice 4)
Modeling vibrating membranes, wave and heat equations (Practice 6)
assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by long answer tests (75%) and a combination of tests, reports, and experimental work (25%). A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required for each assessment component. Both assessment components are recoverable.
